description:
MEASURED by the fz-kdt.125 build (2026-09-01, base bd03d922e): the corpus's
FIFO-vs-LIFO backend-dump population goes 3 -> 4. Base differs on
00277_enum_tier0_fixture, behavior/dead_closure_capture_empty_list and
behavior/enum_map_family; head adds behavior/enum_predicate_search, which is
one of canon_test's four LENSES and whose doc claims byte-identical dumps
either way.

WHAT MOVES: 28 lines, all in ONE List.reduce_while_step/3 call dispatch. Its
two arms swap positions:

  narrow  ({:halt, :false},                 #closure[Enum.empty?/1#lambda])
  wide    ({:cont, :true} | {:halt, :false}, #closure[Enum.all?/1#lambda] |
                                             #closure[Enum.all?/2#lambda] |
                                             #closure[Enum.empty?/1#lambda])

These are the two arms fz-kdt.125 RESTORED: at base they projected to one
runtime question, so fz-kdt.118 dropped the narrow one and the pair had no
order to disagree about. With the callable axis they ask different questions,
both stay, and their arrival order is the semantic fixpoint's -- which is the
agenda's.

NOT a wrong answer, and not the fz-kdt.107 class: the narrow arm's domain is
CONTAINED in the wide arm's on every observable axis, so the narrow test
matches only values its own domain names and the rest fall through. Whichever
order they are tested in, every value lands in an arm whose domain contains it
-- order costs precision here, not meaning. Measured: corpus stdout is
byte-identical FIFO vs LIFO at head (0 movers / 580 fixtures, interp) and
`compiler2_dispatch_answers_the_same_under_a_reversed_arm_order` is green.

THE FREEDOM TO REMOVE: sibling executables already break their tie on
`Types::cmp_tys` (`sibling_specializations_are_ordered_by_canonical_inputs_
not_interning_order`); dispatch ARMS have no such rule. The obvious candidate
is `Order::Specificity`, which the dispatch matrix already models: order a
callsite's DISTINGUISHABLE arms narrow-first on the observable containment
order, and leave a runtime-indistinguishable group in arrival order. That
carve-out matters -- fz-kdt.107 prototyped and REFUTED canonically ordering
INDISTINGUISHABLE arms (4 lib failures incl. {:done,3} for {:halted,3}), and
this proposal must not re-open it. Price the corpus canon movement before
building: every fixture with nested arms would renumber its body ids.
title: A dispatch's distinguishable arms are ordered by arrival, and one lens can now see the schedule
